# Sources and references

## Project basis

Basis of work Puzzle corpus, released plan and stories from the project Git Analyze; unchanged reference copies under conception/. Fictitious Persons and Action. The investigation windows are hypotheses, no proven historical cycles. The XML examples and figures are artificial demonstrations.

## Technical references

- [TEI: Using the Guidelines](https://tei-c.org/release/doc/tei-p5-doc/en/html/USE.html): Policies, Adaptation and Modeling.
- [TEI: item](https://tei-c.org/release/doc/tei-p5-doc/en/html/ref-item.html): List element; the complete document structure must be observed.
- [oXygen Git Client](https://www.oxygenxml.com/doc/ug-addons/git-client/git-addon.html): Integration of version management.
- [GitHub: Releases](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases): releases refer to tags and supplement publication information.
- [Zenodo: GitHub integration](https://help.zenodo.org/docs/github/): Integration for software releases. A suitable publication of research data, metadata and license must be checked separately.
- [Zenodo: DOI versioning](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1256592): version identifiers and cross-version reference.
- [W3C: XSLT 3.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/xslt-30/): Transformations. The local demonstration uses XSLT 1.0 with lxml, not an XSLT-3.0 engine.

## Illustrations

Four specially created AI illustrations (21 October 2026): fundstueck.webp, vergleich.webp. übergabe.webp; seminar.webp: No historical facsimiles and no portraits of real project members. [Full Picture Prompts](assets/bildprompts.md). Diagrams are generated as SVG from the common graph model; tables and demonstration numbers are based on the supplied artificial data.


## Additions to the new conception

- [W3C: XQuery 3.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/xquery-31/): Querying structured data; a query and a schema/content check have different tasks.
- [Python: ElementTree](https://docs.python.org/3/library/xml.etree.elementtree.html): XML processing with the default library, used in the new local entry.
- [GitHub: large files](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/managing-large-files/about-large-files-on-github): Limits of regular Git repos; Customize package and archive concept to data volumes.

New riddle texts and scripts in the start of use are marked as artificial CC0 demonstration. The seminar scene was also created specifically; prompt see image prompts. Research and conference actions are part of the case history.


## File Names and Repo Accompanying Files (0.4)

- [Microsoft: Naming Files, Paths, and Namespaces](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file): problematic characters, reserved device names and caption limits. The project also sets a stricter uniform naming convention.
- [GitHub: README](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-readmes): Entry, benefit, use and care information.
- [Citation File Format: schema Guide](https://github.com/citation-file-format/citation-file-format/blob/main/schema-guide.md): structured citation metadata and resource types.
- [Choose a License](https://choosealicense.com/): Overview of licenses; usage rights and scope are clarified for actual data and tools.

The concrete repo structures, care procedures and file name rules are the developed pattern for Rätselhaft!; they are not an assertion of a compelling universal repo structure.
